findings.issue: Task 6 AC states 'test ctor MUST delegate to the prod ctor via this(...)' — this is backwards. In the actual TelegramSender.java, the PROD (@Autowired) constructor at lines 74-82 is the thin wrapper that delegates to the package-private test constructor via this(builder, baseUrl, DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, DEFAULT_OVERALL_TIMEOUT, ...). The test ctor (88-110) is the FULL implementation. Making the test ctor call this(...) toward the prod ctor would create a circular delegation. The correct instruction is: append SubscriberService to the FULL (package-private) test ctor parameter list; the prod ctor already delegates to it and should also pass the new param.
findings.fix: In task AC and Details, invert the delegation direction: 'prod ctor is a thin wrapper that calls this(builder, baseUrl, DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT, DEFAULT_OVERALL_TIMEOUT, ..., subscriberService). The package-private test ctor carries the full wiring body.' Update 'test ctor delegates to prod ctor via this(...)' to 'prod ctor delegates to test ctor via this(...)'.

findings.issue: SubscriberService interface (backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/subscriber/SubscriberService.java) currently only declares upsertFromTelegramUpdate and markUnsubscribed. The methods markBlockedByChatId and markDeletedByChatId do NOT exist yet — they are added by Task 3 via extending the interface. Task 6 depends_on: [1, 3], which is correct. However, the 'Code files to read' section lists SubscriberService.java and says 'markBlockedByChatId / markDeletedByChatId added by Task 3 (Wave 1 dependency)' — but Task 3 is Wave 2 (not Wave 1). This wave label in the task description is wrong and could confuse implementors about execution order.
findings.fix: In Task 6 'Code files to read' section, fix the parenthetical from 'Wave 1 dependency' to 'Wave 2 dependency (must be merged before Task 6 starts)'. The depends_on: [1, 3] header is already correct.

findings.issue: Task 4 'What to do' step 1 for updateLabel instructs: 'mongoTemplate.update with Update().set("label", label).set("updatedAt", Instant.now())'. The Tag entity data model in tech-spec does NOT include an updatedAt field — the model declares only: id, projectId, slug, label, subscriberCount, createdAt. Setting a non-mapped field via MongoTemplate will write it to the Mongo document but it won't be mapped back to the entity class, creating a schema inconsistency and a phantom field in the collection.
findings.fix: Remove .set("updatedAt", Instant.now()) from the updateLabel instruction, or explicitly add an updatedAt field to the Tag entity data model in the tech-spec and propagate it to the Tag.java definition in Task 1.

findings.issue: Task 5 step 4 instructs the SubscriberCustomFieldsController PATCH endpoint to emit the 'subscriber_custom_field_set' event by calling 'add void recordCustomFieldsSet(String subscriberId, Map<String, Object> values) to SubscriberService interface OR coordinate with Task 3'. Task 5 has depends_on: [1] only, but Task 3 is the owner of SubscriberServiceImpl and any new interface method additions. Both are Wave 2 tasks running in parallel. If Task 5 is merged before Task 3, the interface method won't exist, causing compilation failure. The task text acknowledges this with 'coordinate with Task 3 owner' but offers two compile-time workarounds (a) stub on NoOpSubscriberService or (b) direct write with TODO — neither is formally tracked in depends_on.
findings.fix: Either add Task 3 to depends_on of Task 5 (making it [1, 3]), or clearly designate one of the two fallback paths (a or b) as the canonical approach instead of leaving it open. The current wording creates an undefined build state for the implementor.

findings.issue: Task 6 'What to do' step 3 says 'Promote the Bot bot local at TelegramSender.java:122 to method scope' — but line 122 is the start of the try-block, and Bot bot is declared on line 122 as a local inside the try. The catch block (131-139) currently has no access to it. The task correctly identifies the fix needed. However, step 3 also says 'the catch block reads bot.getProjectId() only on the new TelegramSendException branch (where bot is guaranteed non-null because the exception originated post-load)'. This claim is INCORRECT: if botRepository.findById(botId) throws (network error, Mongo down), bot would be null AND the exception would be a RuntimeException that is NOT a TelegramSendException, so the instanceof check naturally filters it. But if botRepository.findById returns empty and orElseThrow fires an AppException(404), that is also not a TelegramSendException. The safety claim is valid but the reasoning given is slightly incomplete — AppException is also RuntimeException but not TelegramSendException. The null-check defensive comment in the implementation hints (Details section) correctly handles this. Minor correctness issue in step 3 reasoning only.
findings.fix: Amend step 3 to state: 'bot is guaranteed non-null when the instanceof TelegramSendException check succeeds because AppException (404 from orElseThrow) and IllegalStateException (decrypt failure) are excluded by the instanceof filter.' The implementation hint already has this right.

findings.issue: The TDD Anchor for Task 5 includes 'parallel21Posts_acceptsOnly20' (Decision 3 race test) using ConcurrencyTestUtils.parallelInvoke(21, ...). The test description says 'asserts persisted size == 20 exactly, exactly one POST returns 422'. For this to be unambiguous the 21 POSTs must use distinct field names (f1..f21), otherwise name-collision returns 409 (custom_field_name_taken) instead of 422 (custom_field_limit_reached), making the 'exactly one 422' assertion flaky. The task text does say 'design test with distinct names f1..f21' in the Edge Cases section — but this constraint is not stated in the TDD Anchor itself, only in Edge Cases.
findings.fix: Add 'Use distinct names f1..f21 to ensure 409 (name_taken) is not confused with 422 (limit_reached)' to the TDD Anchor entry for parallel21Posts_acceptsOnly20.
